fatal_errors: The proposed material is Q235 carbon steel, whereas the target system is an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L stainless steel.
The central intervention—atmospheric plasma spraying followed by 2 h annealing, particularly at 550 °C—is entirely absent.
The proposed 20–100 °C humidity exposure does not represent the target electrochemical test in 3.5 wt% H2SO4 or the 900 °C cyclic molten-salt tests.
No evidence or citations support the claimed temperature, humidity, oxide-protection relationship, or selected boundaries.
The experiment varies temperature and humidity without a factorial control strategy and therefore does not cleanly isolate a governing cause.

The falsification rule is not decisive: a nominally protective oxide can form while corrosion still increases because protection is relative, transient, porous, cracked, or overwhelmed by harsher exposure.
explanation: The response offers only a generic oxidation/passivation hypothesis. Its limited agreement with the target is the broad idea that an oxide layer can suppress corrosion and that corrosion rate and oxide structure are relevant measurements. It does not reconstruct the coated SS316L system, APS deposition, annealing series, 550 °C optimum, BCC/FCC and grain-boundary mediators, electrochemical acid exposure, or 900 °C Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot corrosion. It also omits the required comparisons with uncoated and as-sprayed references, quantitative predictions, phase and microstructure characterization, and the evidence caveat that the source was retracted. Consequently, it is neither an exact nor partial reconstruction and lacks enough evidence and experimental specificity to qualify as a well-supported alternative.
